title: Robotics benchmarking: where we are, and what comes next
gist: A ProjectSim review of robotics manipulation benchmarks (YCB, LIBERO, RoboCasa365, BEHAVIOR 1K, RoboArena etc.) argues physical robot evaluation is far harder to reproduce than LLM evaluation, and that benchmarks should next guide the costly choice of what training data to collect. ProjectSim's first experiment tests whether higher-fidelity simulated assets and scenes narrow the real-to-sim gap in policy performance.

themes.theme: Composition and robustness gaps in robot policies

insights.claim: In RoboCasa365, GR00T N1.5 fine-tuned on 30,000 demonstrations across 300 tasks averaged 43% success on individual-skill tasks, 9.6% on skill combinations seen in training, and 4.4% on unseen combinations.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Shows state-of-the-art robot foundation models remain far from reliable multi-step household performance, tempering commercialization timelines.
insights.quote: Its average success rate was 43% on tasks built around individual skills, 9.6% on tasks combining skills

insights.claim: In LIBERO Plus, some policies kept performing familiar tasks with an empty instruction and often acted on the original object when the instruction changed the target, revealing weak instruction following masked by high success rates.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Headline benchmark success can overstate true language-conditioned capability of vision-language-action models.
insights.quote: some evaluated policies continued to perform familiar tasks when the instruction was left empty
insights.locator: An apparently successful robot may also rely

insights.claim: A policy can complete many tasks in familiar conditions and still fail when the camera moves, so robustness benchmarks like LIBERO Plus and Colosseum V2 report the effect of each specified change.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Robustness to deployment variation is the real bottleneck for commercial robots, not lab success rates.
insights.quote: A policy can complete many tasks in familiar conditions and still fail when the camera moves.
insights.locator: LIBERO Plus and Colosseum V2 test robustness

insights.claim: A single overall average score would conceal where policies break down; separate scores per ability (components, full tasks, unfamiliar conditions, combinations) answer different questions.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Investors should scrutinize disaggregated metrics rather than aggregate success claims from robotics companies.
insights.quote: The separate scores make that difference visible; one overall average would conceal it.

themes.theme: Physical evaluation is the reproducibility bottleneck

insights.claim: Unlike LLM evaluation (e.g., SWE bench), a physical robot test cannot be reproduced by sharing a policy and code, because camera calibration, gripper pads, table surface and object placements all change outcomes and replaying commands will not recreate a trial.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Robotics lacks the fast, cheap iteration loop that drove LLM progress, slowing capability gains and raising costs.
insights.quote: Replaying the original commands will not recreate the original trial.
insights.locator: Suppose a bowl starts a little farther

insights.claim: The DROID dataset's 76,000 demonstrations (350 hours of interaction) took 50 people across 13 institutions a year to collect, illustrating the scale of physical data effort.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Physical data collection is labor-intensive and expensive, a structural moat and cost center for robotics players.
insights.quote: took 50 people across 13 institutions a year to collect

insights.claim: The author argues robotics needs substantially more investment in physical data collection and in maintaining setups for continued testing.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Signals capital demand for robotics data infrastructure and evaluation services.
insights.quote: This is why robotics needs substantially more investment in this work

insights.claim: Shared remote physical evaluation is emerging: RoboChallenge evaluates submitted policies remotely on common real robots, and RoboArena aggregates blind pairwise comparisons across multiple sites into a ranking.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Evaluation-as-a-service for robotics is a nascent infrastructure niche.

insights.claim: Dataset reuse is hampered by missing task annotations, ambiguous camera labels and inconsistent action formats, per the LeRobot dataset team; evaluation datasets must also document which objects, rooms and tasks were excluded from training.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Standardization of robot data formats is a leverage point for ecosystem players like Hugging Face's LeRobot.
insights.locator: The recordings also need enough documentation

themes.theme: Benchmarks as a guide for data collection

insights.claim: The author proposes that benchmarks should help decide what a policy practises next, providing evidence for one of the most expensive decisions in robot learning: what data to collect next.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Targeted data collection could materially lower the cost curve of training robot policies.
insights.quote: This would give us evidence for one of the most expensive decisions in robot learning: what data to collect next.
insights.locator: What robotics benchmarks should tell us next

insights.claim: In LIBERO RECOVER, adding recovery examples helped policies when placed directly into a failure state but made little difference when policies started from the beginning and encountered their own mistakes.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Naive targeted data does not automatically transfer; measuring what policies actually learn is essential.
insights.quote: They made little difference when policies attempted tasks from the beginning

themes.theme: Real-to-sim gap as the lever for scale

insights.claim: ProjectSim's first experiment tests whether more faithful assets and scenes (geometry, appearance, mass, friction, Gaussian-splat backgrounds) bring simulated policy performance closer to physical results scored by an external evaluator on a two-arm setup.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: High-fidelity sim reconstruction is a potential picks-and-shovels business for robot learning.
insights.locator: This draws on work such as SIMPLER

insights.claim: The author predicts that if realistic simulation holds up, a test-then-practise cycle could run at a scale physical data collection alone cannot support, but notes using reconstructions to improve policy learning is still an unexplored next step.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
insights.so_what: Sim-to-real fidelity would unlock scalable robot training data, a key unlock for the humanoid/manipulation sector.
insights.quote: With realistic simulation, that cycle could run at a scale that physical data collection alone cannot support.
